from: September book, night 28 (The Desert Will Blossom)
p1: Much of Isaiah’s land was desert, dry and sandy, with very few plants.
Isaiah said, “The desert shall rejoice, and blossom as the rose.” Picture dry sand bursting with roses! Water would break out, and thirsty ground would become a pool.
Isaiah’s picture showed that the Lord can make dry, sad places new.
p2: Isaiah said the blind would see and the deaf would hear. People who could not walk would leap like a deer! Many years later, Jesus did these things. He said, “The blind receive their sight, and the lame walk.”
Open your hands like a flower. Jesus heals hearts and bodies. He can make sad places bloom with joy.
old: Isaiah painted the most beautiful picture of hope. He told about a dry, empty desert — and then something wonderful happened!
“The desert will be glad,” Isaiah said, “and the dry, thirsty ground will burst into bloom with flowers! It will blossom like a beautiful rose.”
Imagine a bare, brown place suddenly filling up with soft green grass, splashing streams, and bright, happy flowers everywhere. That’s what Heavenly Father can do!
Heavenly Father can bring beautiful life to even the driest, saddest places. He turns empty into full, and sad into glad, and brown into bloom.
When your heart feels dry or sad, remember: Heavenly Father can make good things bloom again. With Him, there is always hope for something beautiful.
